status: Segmented-reply P1 locally verified; awaiting independent re-review, not release approval
root_cause: The preceding repair joined reply_segments before full matching a payment question, violating the existing multi-segment reply protocol. Passing isolated questions did not cover greetings plus questions.
change: In the sole fact-requirement function, classify each original segment as a complete payment-preference inquiry or other content. Aggregate requirements across every other segment; do not rewrite, filter or merge the reply or citations.
Greetings require no new templates: they go through the existing fact checks like every other non-question segment. The payment-question grammar was not expanded.
Retain finance context across segments so a later rate/monthly-payment/approval statement cannot pass merely by omitting the word loan. Existing high-risk commitment markers are also checked.
Factual modes and product evidence still take precedence; hard risk, declared fact/source validation, semantic review, Guard, retries and task settlement remain unchanged.

added_tests.details: Two/three segments, greeting before/after inquiry, budget question, arbitrary benign greeting, explicit and implicit finance claims before/after/in the same segment. Original segment arrays and knowledge refs retained.

test_boundary: Actual local C3 ASGI API, SQLite, evidence builder, Brain subprocess, HTTP model boundary and Guard; model/reviewer/customer inputs are artificial. Not live Provider quality evaluation, production validation or physical Windows sending. No production access this round.
before_after: Three positive C3 combinations failed with no reply task before the fix and now create exactly one reply_action/chat_reply task, without handoff. Five negative C3 combinations remain AI_ENGINE_NO_VISIBLE_REPLY/retry_later with zero reply tasks. Removing only the segment aggregation in a temporary runtime reproduces eight failures.
audit_limits: Checks cover the affected segmented finance inquiry/authority path; not an assertion that arbitrary natural language or every repository module is defect-free. Earlier self-audits were incomplete and are superseded by the subsequent independent reviews.
